thread:
maria-wu: heads-up — noticed a perf wobble on the canary using FlashBlend + tiled KV on SM90. latency jump ~20% p50 on long sequences (2k+).
ajay: hmm, which build? triton or native cuda kernel?
maria-wu: triton build v1.12.2 with our FlashBlend variant enabled. fallback to fused-cuda gives normal numbers.
leo: can you paste the perfbot summary?
perfbot: canary 2026-03-04T10:02Z - model: redwood-13b-flashblend - region: us-west2 - p50: 112ms -> 135ms (+20%) - p95: 420ms -> 490ms (+16%) - tokens/sec down ~18%
ajay: interesting. might be a tiling/warp alignment issue on SM90. did you try disabling tiled KV to confirm?
maria-wu: yeah, disabling tiled KV (config: "kv.tiled=false") drops p50 back to 110ms. so tiling interacts badly with triton FlashBlend on SM90.
leo: can you run a tiny profiler snippet? nv-nsight or CupTI timeline for the bad run. look for small kernels spiking.
maria-wu: attached quick nvprof scap: ```
# kernel timeline
FlashBlend_tile_compact_sm90  48.2ms
FlashBlend_main               5.6ms
KV_tile_stream               42.0ms
kv_prefetch                  1.1ms
other kernels                3.2ms
```
ajay: that timeline screams split work: tile compact + kv tile stream both expensive. on SM80 we saw better overlap because of different occupancy.
leo: do we have divergent path in FlashBlend when tiled kv present? maybe conditional codegen path in triton emits extra syncs.
maria-wu: grepping generated kernels shows a conditional `if (use_tiled_kv) { sync_local(); }` introduced in flashblend_triton.cpp line ~312. i'll throw a patch to remove the redundant sync as a quick test.
perfbot: note: the commit that introduced that sync was 9f3a7c8 (flashblend: add kv tiling support) in Jan 2026.
ajay: that matches. on SM90 the extra sync kills latency benefits because wavefronts are larger and scheduling differs. on SM80 the sync less harmful.
leo: quick repro plan: (1) baseline binary (triton v1.11 + old flashblend) (2) triton v1.12 w/ sync removed (3) triton v1.12 current. run microbench for seq len 2048, batch 1-8 and measure p50/p95 + kernel events.
maria-wu: running now for batches 1,4,8. will post numbers in ~20m.
(maria-wu adds a short log)
maria-wu: results preliminary: current: p50 b1=135ms b4=160ms. patch: p50 b1=112ms b4=140ms. baseline old triton: p50 b1=110ms b4=138ms.
ajay: nice, removes regression. can we add a guard that's arch-aware instead of dropping sync globally? e.g., `if (use_tiled_kv && arch_sm >= 90) skip_sync()` or better invert logic.
leo: prefer to gate by triton codegen feature flag rather than arch check; but arch check is quicker. also run memory and L2 metrics — tiling changed access patterns maybe thrashing L2 on SM90.
maria-wu: ran nsight L2 counters: L2 hit ratio dropped from 82% -> 67% with tiled KV on current. patch restored to ~80%.
ajay: ok that explains bandwidth blowup. removing sync likely improved scheduling and allowed prefetching to happen earlier so cache got warm.
leo: follow-ups: (1) make patch with conditional no-sync for sm90, (2) add unit test that runs small timeline check ensuring no extra global sync when tiling enabled on sm90, (3) run full canary across regions.
maria-wu: opened PR #3142 with the no-sync option and perf numbers. cc @ajay @leo.
perfbot: canary scheduled for PR 3142 at 2026-03-04T11:30Z.
deploy-bot: canary started: 3142-canary-02 in us-west2. monitor channel for alerts.
ajay: also note: we should add an autotune knob for batching heuristics - on SM90 batched runs with tiled KV need slightly higher max_batch to amortize overhead. add to Optimize suggestions later.
leo: good idea. also run comparison between triton kernel and our CUDA fused variant with the tile path toggled so we have clear perf delta table for docs.
maria-wu: will collect a 3-column table (SM80 triton / SM90 triton / SM90 cuda-fused) and attach to the PR.
ajay: thanks team. great sleuthing. :trophy:
maria-wu: thanks — will follow up once canary finishes.
